pos.personaBrief: Bilardo's Argentina 1986 was built on a defensive platform with Maradona freed, valuing the result over possession; a pragmatic, reactive side (SI/Wilson, TFT).

pro.personaBrief: Pragmatic anti-futbol, few touches to goal and no cult of patient build-up; safe ball-winners like Batista and Maradona freed up front (Wilson, TFT).

est.personaBrief: Heavily drilled, rehearsed positions and fixed roles (Libero, two markers, ball-winner) with video and blackboard work; not a rondo-style relational team (Libero, Wilson).

lar.personaBrief: 3-5-2 with no wingers, wide men as defensive wing-backs, Maradona central; Wilson notes a side with wingers might have overrun them.

blo.personaBrief: Defensive solidity with a libero and markers; knew when to press and when to fall back (Topmercato), with defensive compactness and little forward pressing evidence.

mar.personaBrief: Dedicated man-markers on opposing centre-forwards (Cuciuffo, Ruggeri) and corner moves drilled by marking opponents (TFT).

pla.personaBrief: Obsessive opponent analysis and adaptation (switch vs England, videos), though he imposed his own model on the squad.

res.personaBrief: Football is played to win, shows are for the theater; gamesmanship and win at any price (SI, TFT, CV).

sis.personaBrief: System first: the defensive platform let Maradona roam, but the whole is more important than individuals (Libero 2022) and Bilardo drilled the plan.

jog.personaBrief: Stated that modern football is about running and technique is a foreign word; picked solid ball-winners and aerial/set-piece battles.

bas.personaBrief: Experienced squads in 1986 and a view that Primera is not for learning; youth was secondary to winning.

lid.personaBrief: Moral authority and discipline, called Maradona captain by his own decision over criticism; but the star was treated specially.
